heroLead: East View is a small residential community on the edge of Clarksburg in Harrison County, where mineral tracts often trace back to farmland absorbed as the city expanded outward.
intro: As Clarksburg grew, surrounding farmland like the acreage around East View was gradually subdivided for housing, and in many cases the mineral rights were reserved separately by the selling family rather than conveyed along with the surface. That leaves a mineral estate that doesn't correspond to any current residential lot, tracked instead against the original tract description.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around East View directly, tracing your specific interest back through Harrison County's deed record before making an offer.

sections.heading: Residential growth over an older mineral estate
paragraphs: A homeowner in East View today may have no mineral rights at all if a prior family reserved them at the time of subdivision. We confirm the reservation deed to identify the actual current mineral owner before evaluating an interest.

sections.heading: Harrison County leasing reaches the Clarksburg suburbs
paragraphs: Operators active in Harrison County haven't confined leasing to open farmland; suburban-adjacent tracts around East View can still be pulled into modern units, particularly where acreage from several original farms was combined.

sections.heading: Confirming the reservation and current ownership
paragraphs: We check the original severance deed, any subsequent transfers, and current lease or unit status before pricing your East View-area mineral interest.

Because subdivision paperwork rarely draws attention to a mineral reservation buried in an earlier deed, this step often surfaces details neither the current surface owner nor the mineral-owning family had connected before.

faqs.question: I bought a house in East View. Do I own any mineral rights under it?
faqs.answer: Possibly not, if a prior owner reserved the minerals when the land was subdivided. We can check the recorded history for your specific lot.

faqs.question: My family reserved the minerals decades ago when we sold land near East View. Are they still ours?
faqs.answer: Likely yes, provided the reservation was properly recorded and passed correctly through any subsequent estates.

faqs.question: Is there active leasing in this part of Harrison County?
faqs.answer: It varies by tract. We check current lease and unit records covering your specific mineral interest as part of our review.

faqs.question: What documents help confirm a mineral reservation from a subdivision sale?
faqs.answer: The original deed from the sale, if you have it, is useful, but we can locate the recorded instrument at the Harrison County Clerk's office if you don't.
